title: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants
seo_title: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants Class 12 Biology Worksheet (NCERT Ch 1)
standard_code: Class 12 Biology, Chapter 1: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants
standard_text: Flower structure; development of male and female gametophytes; pollination – types, agencies and examples; out breeding devices; pollen–pistil interaction; double fertilization; post fertilization events – development of endosperm and embryo, development of seed and formation of fruit; special modes – apomixis, parthenocarpy, polyembryony; significance of seed dispersal and fruit formation.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Biology worksheets for NCERT Chapter 1 Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants: stamen and pistil, pollen and embryo sac, pollination, outbreeding devices, double fertilisation, seeds, fruits and apomixis. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Endosperm is triploid; the zygote is diploid.
body_html:
How to think about it

The stamen (anther and filament) makes pollen grains, each with a vegetative cell and a generative cell inside a tough exine of sporopollenin. The pistil (stigma, style, ovary) holds ovules; a megaspore develops into a 7-celled, 8-nucleate embryo sac. Pollen reaches the stigma by self-pollination (autogamy, geitonogamy) or cross-pollination (xenogamy) carried by wind, water or animals; outbreeding devices prevent selfing.

In double fertilisation one male gamete fuses with the egg (syngamy, forming the zygote) and the other with the two polar nuclei (triple fusion, forming the triploid endosperm). The ovule becomes the seed and the ovary the fruit. Apomixis gives seeds without fertilisation; parthenocarpy gives seedless fruits.

Example

Ploidy of the endosperm?

2 polar nuclei + 1 gamete

Answer: 3n

Example

Pollen to another flower on the same plant?

same plant

Answer: geitonogamy

Common mistakes

  • Calling geitonogamy cross-pollination genetically.
  • Saying the embryo sac has 8 cells.
  • Mixing up the coleoptile and coleorhiza.
